title: The Ferryman Who Took a Slice
story: The flooded reed-road is crossable only by Skarrowbend's creaking ferry, and the old tollkeep charges a share of every cargo instead of coins. Twelve families are waiting with sacks of silverseed to sell at the upriver fair. Mr 6 hops aboard and politely asks to see the toll scroll.
question: The families have 480 pounds of silverseed. Skarrowbend takes 25% of it as the crossing toll, then a second 10% of whatever remains as a "reed-bending fee." How many pounds of silverseed do the families still have after both tolls?
solution: The first toll takes 480 x 0.25 = 120 pounds, leaving 480 - 120 = 360 pounds.
The second fee takes 10% of 360, which is 36 pounds.
360 - 36 = 324 pounds of silverseed are left for the families.
praise: Taking the percents one at a time was smart thinking — the second fee just had to come off the smaller pile, not the original 480.
hint: Find the pile that is left after the first toll, then take 10% of THAT number, not of 480.
victory: Mr 6 read the toll scroll aloud twice, and Skarrowbend — caught charging fees on sacks he had already taxed — poled everyone across for free and threw in a basket of river pears.
imagePrompt: A stooped, reed-cloaked tollkeep with a long pole on a wooden ferry in a misty flooded marsh, as a small numeral-6 knight holds up a tattered toll scroll in the grey dawn light.
